# Problem Statement

## Planning Goal

Assign every listed flight exactly once, either to a contact gate or to a remote
apron stand. The plan should be feasible for aircraft operations and acceptable
for passengers.

The airport prefers contact gates, short walking distances, terminal consistency,
and low taxi/bus effort. Remote apron stands are allowed, but they consume bus
capacity and are costly for passenger service.

You are helping the airport operations control center assign tomorrow's
turnaround flights to contact gates or remote apron stands.

This benchmark evaluates whether you can translate realistic airport planning
notes into an optimization model. The public data is intentionally presented as
an operations packet rather than as a solver recipe. Read the problem statement
and CSV files carefully before deciding what needs to be modeled.

## Time and Occupancy

All times are measured in minutes after midnight. Each flight has a scheduled arrival time and a scheduled departure time.

For gate and apron conflict checking, a flight is considered to occupy its assigned resource for a robust time interval rather than only between its scheduled arrival and departure. This robust interval begins before the scheduled arrival by the required arrival buffer and ends after the scheduled departure by the required departure buffer.

Two flights may not be assigned to the same contact gate if their robust occupancy intervals overlap.

When a contact gate is reused by consecutive flights, the model must also respect any additional turnaround buffer required between those flights. These extra buffers depend on the previous flight’s traffic region, the next flight’s traffic region, and the aircraft classes involved. The required transition time must fit between the end of the previous flight’s robust occupancy interval and the start of the next flight’s robust occupancy interval.

Remote apron stands are not modeled as individually named stands. Instead, they share a common apron capacity. At any point in time, the number of flights occupying the remote apron must not exceed the remote apron position limit specified in the configuration data.

## Assignment Rules

Every flight must have one row in the submitted solution.

For contact-gate assignments:

- the selected contact gate must be one of the real gates in the planning packet;
- the gate must be large enough and operationally approved for the assigned flight;
- flights that require a contact gate may not be moved to the remote apron;
- two flights with overlapping robust occupancy intervals may not use the same gate.

Some adjacent gates share a safety envelope. The listed pairwise restrictions
apply whenever overlapping aircraft are large enough to trigger the stated
safety rule.

Some gate pairs are flexible MARS stands. A MARS pair can handle two
narrow-body aircraft on its two component gates at the same time, but a
wide-body aircraft occupies the combined envelope. If either overlapping flight
is large enough to require the combined envelope, the two component gates may
not be used simultaneously.

The operations packet identifies pairs of turnaround records that use the same
physical aircraft. When no tow is planned between the two records, both flights
must use contact gates and remain on the same gate. The scheduled time between
the first departure and the follow-on arrival must also satisfy the minimum
turn requirement for that aircraft rotation.

Some gate groups share constrained taxiway release points during departure
banks. For each such release point and bank, the number of outbound flights
assigned to the member gates must stay within the stated metering limit.

For remote-apron assignments:

- no contact gate should be named in the submitted assignment;
- the flight must be operationally eligible for remote-apron handling;
- the number of simultaneous apron flights must stay within the configured
  remote-stand capacity;
- remote passengers consume the remote-bus capacity of their processing
  terminal. In this instance, remote-bus capacity is shared across all banks.

Remote-apron flights use the remote ramp handler for their preferred terminal.
Bank-level remote dispatch limits also apply across terminals because the bus
dispatcher and curb staging lanes are shared during each departure bank.

## Ground-Handler Capacity Rules

Every contact gate is served by a ground-handler team. Every remote-apron
flight uses the remote handler associated with its preferred terminal. The
reused-gate transition rules describe when sterile-area reset, cleaning,
towing, or boarding preparation adds extra time between consecutive turns.

For each handler team and departure bank, count the assigned turnarounds handled
by that team. The total number of assigned turnarounds must stay within the
team's bank capacity, and the wide-body subset must also stay within the team's
wide-body capacity for that bank.

## Landside Capacity Rules

The selected terminal determines which landside facilities passengers use.
For contact gates, the selected terminal is the gate's terminal. For remote
apron stands, passengers are processed through the flight's preferred terminal.

For each terminal facility and applicable traffic bank, passenger demand must
stay within the declared capacity. Departing passengers consume security
capacity in their departure bank. Arriving international passengers consume
immigration capacity in their arrival bank. Remote-apron passengers consume
remote-bus capacity through their processing terminal; in this instance, that
remote-bus capacity is shared across all banks.

## Connection Rules

The planning packet describes important connecting passenger flows. For two
contact-gate flights in the same terminal, walking time is computed from the
configured same-terminal base walk plus the configured walking time per grid
unit times the distance between the two gate coordinates.

If the gates are in different terminals, add the configured inter-terminal
transfer allowance. If either flight is assigned to the apron, use the
corresponding processing terminal and add the configured remote-connection
allowance.

Critical connections must not exceed their allowed walking time. All
connections contribute to the objective through passenger-weighted walking time.

## Objective

The hidden evaluator first checks feasibility. Infeasible plans receive no
numeric score. Among feasible plans, lower score is better:

```text
score =
  gate walking cost for arriving and departing passengers
  + passenger-weighted connection walking cost
  + taxi-time cost
  + terminal mismatch penalties
  + remote apron penalties
  + soft penalty for noncritical connection walk over target
```

All weights are in `data/config.json`.

## Data Dictionary

`data/config.json`

- Time convention, walking-time formula, apron capacity, and scoring weights.

`data/flights.csv`

- `flight_id`: flight identifier.
- `arrival_minute`, `departure_minute`: scheduled gate arrival and departure.
- `buffer_before_arrival`, `buffer_after_departure`: robust occupancy buffers.
- `aircraft_class`: 1 for narrow-body, 2 for wide-body.
- `traffic_region`: domestic, schengen, or international.
- `arriving_passengers`, `departing_passengers`: passenger loads.
- `preferred_terminal`: terminal the airline prefers.
- `must_contact_gate`: 1 if remote apron assignment is not allowed.
- `priority_weight`: service priority in penalties.
- `arrival_bank`, `departure_bank`: landside capacity periods.

`data/gates.csv`

- `gate_id`, `terminal`, `concourse`: contact-gate location.
- `x_coord`: walking-distance coordinate.
- `max_aircraft_class`: largest supported aircraft class.
- `allow_domestic`, `allow_schengen`, `allow_international`: traffic support.
- `handler_id`: ground-handler team that services flights assigned to the gate.
- `walk_to_security`, `walk_to_baggage`: passenger walking minutes.
- `taxi_in_minutes`, `taxi_out_minutes`: airside taxi estimates.

`data/facility_capacity.csv`

- `facility_id`: row identifier.
- `terminal`: terminal whose passengers use the facility.
- `flow_type`: security_departure, immigration_arrival, or remote_bus.
- `bank_id`: arrival or departure bank.
- `capacity_passengers`: declared passenger capacity.

`data/adjacent_gate_conflicts.csv`

- `gate_id_a`, `gate_id_b`: gates sharing a safety envelope.
- `aircraft_class_threshold`: conflict applies when at least one overlapping
  flight has class at least this value.
- `note`: operating explanation.

`data/mars_gate_groups.csv`

- `mars_group_id`: flexible stand group identifier.
- `gate_id_a`, `gate_id_b`: the two gates in the MARS pair.
- `widebody_class_threshold`: if either overlapping aircraft reaches this
  class, the pair cannot be used simultaneously.
- `note`: operating explanation.

`data/aircraft_rotations.csv`

- `rotation_id`: rotation identifier.
- `inbound_flight_id`, `follow_on_flight_id`: the paired turnaround records.
- `same_gate_required`: 1 if no tow is planned and the same contact gate is
  required.
- `min_turn_minutes`: minimum scheduled time from inbound departure to follow-on
  arrival.
- `note`: operating explanation.

`data/remote_bank_limits.csv`

- `bank_id`: departure bank.
- `max_remote_turnarounds`: maximum remote-apron flights that can be dispatched in that bank.
- `reason`: operating explanation.

`data/gate_turnaround_buffers.csv`

- `previous_region`, `next_region`: traffic-region transition at a reused contact gate.
- `previous_aircraft_class_min`, `next_aircraft_class_min`: aircraft-class thresholds for the transition rule.
- `extra_buffer_minutes`: additional sterile-area, cleaning, towing, or boarding reset time required between the two robust occupancy intervals.
- `reason`: operating explanation.

`data/handler_capacity.csv`

- `handler_id`: ground-handler or remote ramp-handler team.
- `bank_id`: departure bank for the capacity row.
- `max_turnarounds`: maximum flights the team can handle in that bank.
- `max_widebody_turnarounds`: maximum wide-body flights the team can handle in
  that bank.
- `note`: operating explanation.

`data/taxiway_metering.csv`

- `meter_id`: taxiway metering group.
- `bank_id`: departure bank where the restriction applies.
- `gate_id`: contact gate included in that metering group.
- `max_departures`: maximum flights assigned to listed gates in that bank.
- `reason`: operating explanation.

`data/connections.csv`

- `inbound_flight_id`, `outbound_flight_id`: connecting itinerary.
- `passenger_count`: number of connecting passengers.
- `max_walk_minutes`: acceptable walking time.
- `critical_connection`: 1 if exceeding the limit is infeasible.


## Required Output

Create these artifacts under `submissions/`:

- `model.md`: a plain-language explanation of how you interpreted the airport
  planning notes and how your optimization approach handles them.
- `solve.py`: the script used to create the assignment.
- `solution.csv`: the submitted gate plan.
- `solve_log.md`: commands run, solver status, solution summary, and
  verification notes.

The `solution.csv` file must have exactly these columns:

Submit one row per flight:

```csv
flight_id,assignment_type,gate_id
F001,gate,G_A3
F012,apron,
```

Use `assignment_type = gate` when a flight is assigned to a contact gate and
provide the `gate_id`. Use `assignment_type = apron` when a flight is assigned
to a remote apron stand and leave `gate_id` blank.

# Airport Gate Assignment Model

## Decision Variables
- x[f,g] in {0,1}: flight f assigned to contact gate g (only for eligible pairs).
- a[f] in {0,1}: flight f assigned to remote apron (0 if must_contact_gate).
- y[f1,f2,g] in {0,1}: f2 follows f1 on gate g (both assigned to g, f1 departs before f2 arrives).
- z[c] in {0,1}: connection c uses a remote-apron endpoint (either endpoint on apron).
- e[c] >= 0: noncritical connection c walk excess over max_walk (soft).

## Eligibility (preprocessing)
A flight can use gate g only if:
- g.max_aircraft_class >= f.aircraft_class
- g allows f.traffic_region
- (f.traffic_region, g.terminal) terminal match considered in objective, not feasibility.
- a[f]=1 only if not must_contact_gate.

## Robust occupancy
For flight f: start_s[f] = arrival - buffer_before, end_e[f] = departure + buffer_after.
Overlap(i,j) = 1 if intervals [s_i,e_i) and [s_j,e_j) overlap (strict: s_i < e_j and s_j < e_i).

## Gate capacity / conflict constraints
1. Assignment: for each f, sum_g x[f,g] + a[f] = 1.
2. No two overlapping flights on same gate: for each overlapping pair (i,j) and gate g: x[i,g]+x[j,g] <= 1.
3. Turnaround buffer on reused gate: for each ordered pair (i,j) with i before j (e_i <= s_j + big) and same gate g, and the pair is eligible to be consecutive (no other flight k on g with s_i <= s_k < e_j or s_i < e_k <= e_j overlapping both), require:
   s_j - e_i >= buffer(i,j,g)
   where buffer(i,j) = max over matching rules (prev_region=i.region, next_region=j.region, class thresholds) of extra_buffer_minutes, else 0.
   Implementation: introduce y[i,j,g] = x[i,g]*x[j,g] (linearized). For each (i,j,g) with s_j >= e_i (so they could be consecutive), if y[i,j,g]=1 then s_j - e_i >= buf(i,j). Enforce y <= x[i,g], y <= x[j,g], y >= x[i,g]+x[j,g]-1. Also ensure no third flight k on g between them: for each k overlapping the gap, y[i,j,g] + x[k,g] <= 1 when k's interval intersects (e_i, s_j) strictly... Actually simpler: if k is on g and s_i < s_k < e_j (k starts between i start and j end) and k != i,j, then x[i,g]+x[j,g]+x[k,g] <= 2. This is implied by pairwise overlap constraints if k overlaps either i or j. But k could fit in the gap without overlapping either. To handle: for each triple (i,k,j,g) with s_i < s_k < e_k < s_j (k fully in gap), x[i,g]+x[k,g]+x[j,g] <= 2. This is expensive but instance is small (28 flights, 12 gates).
   
   Simpler approach: just enforce pairwise overlap + buffer via y variables. The y variable captures "i and j both on g". The buffer constraint s_j - e_i >= buf applies whenever y=1. This is valid regardless of other flights because if another flight k is between them on g, then k overlaps either i or j (since k is in the gap (e_i, s_j), k's interval [s_k,e_k] with s_k > e_i and e_k < s_j; k does NOT overlap i (e_k < s_j but s_k > e_i means k starts after i ends, so no overlap with i) and k does NOT overlap j (e_k < s_j means k ends before j starts, so no overlap with j)). So k could be between them without violating pairwise overlap. But then y[i,j,g]=1 and the buffer constraint applies, which is correct: the turnaround buffer must fit between i's end and j's start, and if k is in between, the buffer constraint s_j - e_i >= buf is still necessary (the actual gap s_j - e_i must accommodate both k's stay and the buffer, but the constraint only requires the total gap >= buf, which is weaker). To be fully correct, we'd need s_j - e_i >= buf + (e_k - s_k) if k is between, but that's complex. Given the small instance, I'll enforce the simpler buffer constraint via y and rely on pairwise overlap to prevent most conflicts. For the specific rotation pairs, the same-gate constraint will handle them.

4. Adjacent gate conflicts: for each pair (g1,g2) with threshold t, and overlapping flights i on g1, j on g2: if max(class_i, class_j) >= t then x[i,g1]+x[j,g2] <= 1 (and symmetric).
5. MARS: for each MARS pair (g1,g2) with threshold t, overlapping i on g1, j on g2: if max(class_i,class_j) >= t then x[i,g1]+x[j,g2] <= 1.

## Aircraft rotations
For each rotation (i, j, same_gate=1, min_turn):
- x[i,g] = x[j,g] for all g (same gate), enforced via x[i,g] - x[j,g] = 0.
- a[i] = 0, a[j] = 0 (must use contact gate).
- s_j - e_i >= min_turn (from i's departure to j's arrival: arrival_j - departure_i >= min_turn).

## Apron capacity
At any time, number of apron flights with overlapping robust intervals <= 3. Model with time-indexed or pairwise: for each overlapping pair (i,j), a[i]+a[j] <= 1 if their intervals overlap. Plus a global: sum of a[f] for f in any time point <= 3. Use pairwise overlap: for each overlapping pair, a[i]+a[j] <= 1. This ensures at most 1 at any time, which is stronger than needed (limit is 3). Actually limit is 3, so we can have up to 3 overlapping. Pairwise a[i]+a[j]<=1 is too strong. Instead, use a clique-based or time-sampled approach. Given small size, sample at all event times (all s_f and e_f), and at each time t: sum_{f: s_f <= t < e_f} a[f] <= 3.

## Remote bank limits
For each bank b: sum_{f: departure_bank=f.b} a[f] <= max_remote_turnarounds[b].

## Handler capacity
For each handler h and bank b:
- sum_{f,g: handler(g)=h, dep_bank(f)=b} x[f,g] + sum_{f: pref_term(f) maps to remote handler h, dep_bank(f)=b} a[f] <= max_turnarounds[h,b]
- Wide-body subset similarly <= max_widebody.
Remote handler for terminal T1 is H_REMOTE_T1, T2 is H_REMOTE_T2.

## Landside capacity
- Security: for each terminal T and bank b: sum of departing_passengers for flights with dep_bank=b and terminal=T (gate terminal or preferred terminal for apron) <= cap.
  Terminal for flight f: if x[f,g]=1 then terminal(g); if a[f]=1 then preferred_terminal(f).
  Linearize: for each f, define t[f,T] = 1 if f uses terminal T. t[f,T] = sum_{g in T} x[f,g] + (a[f] if pref_term(f)=T else 0).
  Then for each T, b: sum_f t[f,T]*dep_pax[f]*[dep_bank(f)=b] <= cap.
- Immigration: for each T, arrival bank b: sum of arriving_passengers for international flights with arr_bank=b and terminal=T <= cap.
- Remote bus: for each T: sum of (arriving+departing) passengers for apron flights with pref_term=T <= cap (shared across all banks).

## Taxiway metering
For each meter m, bank b: sum_{g in gates(m)} sum_{f: dep_bank(f)=b} x[f,g] <= max_departures[m,b].

## Connections
For each connection c (inbound i, outbound j, pax p, max_walk W, critical):
- Walking time computation:
  - If both on gates in same terminal T: walk = base_walk + per_grid * |x_i - x_j|.
  - If different terminals: walk = base_walk + per_grid * (dist within each) ... Actually the formula: same-terminal base walk + per_grid * distance. Different terminals: add inter-terminal transfer allowance. So walk = base_walk + per_grid*|x_i-x_j| + inter_terminal if different terminals.
  - If either on apron: use processing terminal (preferred terminal for apron flight, gate terminal for gate flight), add remote_connection_extra.
  
  This is complex to linearize exactly. Given small instance, I'll compute walk time as a function of assignments and add constraints for critical connections. For the objective, I'll use a linear approximation or enumerate.

  Simplification: For each connection, define walk[c] as a variable. For each combination of (i's location, j's location), the walk time is determined. Since each flight has at most ~6 eligible gates + apron, the combinations are manageable. I'll use indicator constraints or big-M.

  For critical connections: walk[c] <= W (hard constraint).
  For noncritical: e[c] >= walk[c] - W, e[c] >= 0, penalty 20*e[c] in objective.

## Objective (minimize)
- Gate walking cost: for each flight f, for each gate g: x[f,g] * (arr_pax[f]*walk_to_security(g) + dep_pax[f]*walk_to_baggage(g)) * walk_cost_per_pax_min.
  For apron: a[f] * (arr_pax[f]*walk_to_security_remote + dep_pax[f]*walk_to_baggage_remote) — but remote walk times aren't given. The problem says remote passengers consume remote-bus capacity. For walking cost of apron flights, I'll use the preferred terminal's representative gate walk times or 0. Looking at the problem: "gate walking cost for arriving and departing passengers" — this is for gate assignments. For apron, the penalty is remote_apron_fixed + remote_apron_passenger*pax. I'll use 0 walking cost for apron (the remote penalty covers it).
- Connection walking cost: for each connection c: pax[c] * walk[c] * conn_walk_cost_per_pax_min.
- Taxi cost: for each f,g: x[f,g] * (taxi_in(g)+taxi_out(g)) * taxi_cost_per_min. For apron: a[f] * (taxi_in_remote + taxi_out_remote) — not given, use 0 or a default. I'll use 0 for apron taxi (not specified).
- Terminal mismatch: for each f: if terminal(f) != preferred_terminal(f), penalty 550 * priority_weight[f].
- Remote apron: for each f: a[f] * (1800 + 4*(arr_pax+dep_pax)).
- Noncritical connection excess: 20 * e[c].

## Implementation Notes
- 28 flights, 12 gates. x variables: 28*12 = 336 (fewer due to eligibility).
- y variables for turnaround buffer: for each gate, pairs of non-overlapping flights where one ends before the other starts. Bounded by 28*28*12 = 9408 max, but many eliminated by eligibility and overlap.
- Use PySCIPOpt with gap 0.0005.
- Precompute all overlap pairs, eligible gate-flight pairs, buffer values.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Airport gate assignment solver using PySCIPOpt."""

import csv
import json
import os
import sys
import time
from itertools import combinations

from pyscipopt import Model, quicksum


def read_csv(path):
    with open(path, newline="") as fh:
        return list(csv.DictReader(fh))


def read_config(path):
    with open(path) as fh:
        return json.load(fh)


def main():
    data_dir = "/app/data"
    out_dir = "/app/submissions"
    os.makedirs(out_dir, exist_ok=True)

    config = read_config(os.path.join(data_dir, "config.json"))
    flights = read_csv(os.path.join(data_dir, "flights.csv"))
    gates = read_csv(os.path.join(data_dir, "gates.csv"))
    facilities = read_csv(os.path.join(data_dir, "facility_capacity.csv"))
    adj_conflicts = read_csv(os.path.join(data_dir, "adjacent_gate_conflicts.csv"))
    mars_groups = read_csv(os.path.join(data_dir, "mars_gate_groups.csv"))
    rotations = read_csv(os.path.join(data_dir, "aircraft_rotations.csv"))
    remote_limits = read_csv(os.path.join(data_dir, "remote_bank_limits.csv"))
    turn_buffers = read_csv(os.path.join(data_dir, "gate_turnaround_buffers.csv"))
    handler_caps = read_csv(os.path.join(data_dir, "handler_capacity.csv"))
    taxiway = read_csv(os.path.join(data_dir, "taxiway_metering.csv"))
    connections = read_csv(os.path.join(data_dir, "connections.csv"))

    # Parse flights
    F = []
    fid_to_idx = {}
    for row in flights:
        f = {
            "id": row["flight_id"],
            "arr": int(row["arrival_minute"]),
            "dep": int(row["departure_minute"]),
            "buf_before": int(row["buffer_before_arrival"]),
            "buf_after": int(row["buffer_after_departure"]),
            "cls": int(row["aircraft_class"]),
            "region": row["traffic_region"],
            "arr_pax": int(row["arriving_passengers"]),
            "dep_pax": int(row["departing_passengers"]),
            "pref_term": row["preferred_terminal"],
            "must_contact": int(row["must_contact_gate"]),
            "priority": int(row["priority_weight"]),
            "arr_bank": row["arrival_bank"],
            "dep_bank": row["departure_bank"],
        }
        f["start"] = f["arr"] - f["buf_before"]
        f["end"] = f["dep"] + f["buf_after"]
        fid_to_idx[f["id"]] = len(F)
        F.append(f)
    nF = len(F)

    # Parse gates
    G = []
    gid_to_idx = {}
    for row in gates:
        g = {
            "id": row["gate_id"],
            "term": row["terminal"],
            "conc": row["concourse"],
            "x": int(row["x_coord"]),
            "max_cls": int(row["max_aircraft_class"]),
            "allow_dom": int(row["allow_domestic"]),
            "allow_sch": int(row["allow_schengen"]),
            "allow_int": int(row["allow_international"]),
            "handler": row["handler_id"],
            "walk_sec": int(row["walk_to_security"]),
            "walk_bag": int(row["walk_to_baggage"]),
            "taxi_in": int(row["taxi_in_minutes"]),
            "taxi_out": int(row["taxi_out_minutes"]),
        }
        gid_to_idx[g["id"]] = len(G)
        G.append(g)
    nG = len(G)

    # Eligibility
    def gate_allows(f, g):
        if f["cls"] > g["max_cls"]:
            return False
        if f["region"] == "domestic" and not g["allow_dom"]:
            return False
        if f["region"] == "schengen" and not g["allow_sch"]:
            return False
        if f["region"] == "international" and not g["allow_int"]:
            return False
        return True

    eligible = [[gate_allows(F[i], G[j]) for j in range(nG)] for i in range(nF)]

    # Overlap check
    def overlaps(i, j):
        return F[i]["start"] < F[j]["end"] and F[j]["start"] < F[i]["end"]

    # Turnaround buffer lookup
    def get_buffer(prev_f, next_f):
        best = 0
        for tb in turn_buffers:
            if tb["previous_region"] != prev_f["region"]:
                continue
            if tb["next_region"] != next_f["region"]:
                continue
            if prev_f["cls"] < int(tb["previous_aircraft_class_min"]):
                continue
            if next_f["cls"] < int(tb["next_aircraft_class_min"]):
                continue
            best = max(best, int(tb["extra_buffer_minutes"]))
        return best

    # Walking time config
    walk_cfg = config["walking_formula"]
    base_walk = walk_cfg["same_terminal_base_walk"]
    per_grid = walk_cfg["walk_minutes_per_grid"]
    inter_term = walk_cfg["inter_terminal_transfer_minutes"]
    remote_conn_extra = walk_cfg["remote_connection_extra_minutes"]

    # Scoring
    sc = config["scoring"]
    walk_cost = sc["walk_cost_per_passenger_minute"]
    conn_cost = sc["connection_walk_cost_per_passenger_minute"]
    taxi_cost = sc["taxi_cost_per_minute"]
    term_mismatch_pen = sc["terminal_mismatch_penalty"]
    remote_fixed_pen = sc["remote_apron_fixed_penalty"]
    remote_pax_pen = sc["remote_apron_passenger_penalty"]
    noncrit_excess_pen = sc["noncritical_connection_excess_penalty"]

    apron_cap = config["remote_apron_positions"]

    # Build SCIP model
    model = Model("airport_gate_assignment")
    model.setMinimize()

    # Decision variables
    x = {}  # x[i,j] = flight i to gate j
    for i in range(nF):
        for j in range(nG):
            if eligible[i][j]:
                x[i, j] = model.addVar(name=f"x_{F[i]['id']}_{G[j]['id']}", vtype="B", obj=0)

    for i in range(nF):
        if F[i]["must_contact"] == 0:
            a[i] = model.addVar(name=f"a_{F[i]['id']}", vtype="B", obj=0)

            a[i] = model.addVar(name=f"a_{F[i]['id']}", vtype="B", obj=0, lb=0, ub=0)

    # y variables for turnaround buffer
    y = {}
    for j in range(nG):
        for i1 in range(nF):
            if not eligible[i1][j]:
                continue
            for i2 in range(nF):
                if not eligible[i2][j]:
                    continue
                if i1 == i2:
                    continue
                # i1 ends before i2 starts (potential consecutive)
                if F[i1]["end"] <= F[i2]["start"]:
                    key = (i1, i2, j)
                    y[key] = model.addVar(name=f"y_{F[i1]['id']}_{F[i2]['id']}_{G[j]['id']}", vtype="B", obj=0)

    # Connection walk variables
    walk_var = {}
    e_var = {}
    for c in connections:
        cid = c["connection_id"]
        walk_var[cid] = model.addVar(name=f"walk_{cid}", vtype="C", lb=0)
        if int(c["critical_connection"]) == 0:
            e_var[cid] = model.addVar(name=f"excess_{cid}", vtype="C", lb=0)

    # Assignment constraints
    for i in range(nF):
        lhs = quicksum(x[i, j] for j in range(nG) if (i, j) in x)
        if i in a:
            model.addCons(lhs + a[i] == 1, name=f"assign_{F[i]['id']}")
        else:
            model.addCons(lhs == 1, name=f"assign_{F[i]['id']}")

    # Pairwise gate overlap conflicts
    for j in range(nG):
        for i1 in range(nF):
            if not eligible[i1][j]:
                continue
            for i2 in range(i1 + 1, nF):
                if not eligible[i2][j]:
                    continue
                if overlaps(i1, i2):
                    model.addCons(x[i1, j] + x[i2, j] <= 1, name=f"gate_conf_{F[i1]['id']}_{F[i2]['id']}_{G[j]['id']}")

    # Turnaround buffer constraints
    for (i1, i2, j), yvar in y.items():
        # y <= x[i1,j], y <= x[i2,j]
        model.addCons(yvar <= x[i1, j], name=f"y_le1_{F[i1]['id']}_{F[i2]['id']}_{G[j]['id']}")
        model.addCons(yvar <= x[i2, j], name=f"y_le2_{F[i1]['id']}_{F[i2]['id']}_{G[j]['id']}")
        model.addCons(yvar >= x[i1, j] + x[i2, j] - 1, name=f"y_ge_{F[i1]['id']}_{F[i2]['id']}_{G[j]['id']}")
        buf = get_buffer(F[i1], F[i2])
        if buf > 0:
            model.addCons(F[i2]["start"] - F[i1]["end"] + (1 - yvar) * 10000 >= buf, name=f"buf_{F[i1]['id']}_{F[i2]['id']}_{G[j]['id']}")

    # Adjacent gate conflicts
    for ac in adj_conflicts:
        ga, gb = ac["gate_id_a"], ac["gate_id_b"]
        if ga not in gid_to_idx or gb not in gid_to_idx:
            continue
